title: Your Instrument

learn.summary: Theory becomes music only through an instrument — and the best one is the one you will actually pick up daily. Piano makes theory visible, guitar makes chords portable, and your voice is already installed. Access beats prestige: a cheap keyboard in your living room outperforms a grand piano you never visit.

do: Commit in writing to one instrument for the next 90 days, and put it (or the app for it) physically within reach of your sofa today.

children.title: Choosing Honestly

learn.summary: Choose on three honest axes: the sound that gives you chills (motivation fuel), your logistics (space, budget, neighbors), and time-to-gratification. Piano and ukulele reward week one; violin and trumpet punish month three. A 61-key keyboard or a ukulele under modest cost is a serious, legitimate starting instrument.

do: Write a three-line comparison of your top two instrument candidates (sound love, logistics, first-week payoff) and pick the winner by Sunday.

children.title: Voice: the Free Instrument

learn.summary: Your voice is a full instrument with zero cost, zero setup, and total portability — and singing is the most direct ear-training there is, because there are no keys to hide behind. Kodály-based music education starts every child on voice first for exactly this reason. Even confirmed instrumentalists progress faster when they sing their lines.

do: Sing along to three songs in the car or shower this week at full commitment — treat it as practice, not background noise.

children.title: First-Month Reality

learn.summary: Month one sounds bad for everyone — buzzing strings, clunky chord changes, sore fingertips are the curriculum, not a verdict. Fifteen to twenty minutes daily beats two hours on Saturday, because motor skills consolidate between sessions, largely during sleep. Your only real first-month goal: show up daily and play one thing recognizably.

do: Put a calendar checkmark on every day you touch the instrument for 15 minutes — aim for a 6-of-7 streak this week, quality irrelevant.

children.title: Teacher vs Self-Teaching

learn.summary: A teacher's irreplaceable value is catching bad physical habits — tension, posture, thumb position — before they calcify; apps and videos cannot watch your hands. If lessons are out of budget, even a single monthly check-in lesson steers months of self-study. Self-teaching works best with a fixed curriculum (a method book or graded syllabus), not algorithmic video drift.

do: This week either book one trial lesson (many teachers offer them cheap) or choose one method book/course and write down its first four milestones.
